**Answer.** Yes. Evaluating the airframe against both store photographs confirms that the reconstruction holds across all major features (@fig-overlays). While the [initial reconstruction](2026-10-07-01-can-we-reconstruct-the-ft-f-16-viper-within-tolerance.qmd) displayed only the belly frame, the studio perspective reveals the upper surfaces that the ventral view obscured: the bubble canopy height, dorsal spine taper, wing leading-edge strakes, and wingtip missile rail alignment.

The studio pose converges cleanly at camera elevation [20\.0°]{.key}, azimuth [210\.5°]{.key}, and roll [\-12\.8°]{.key}, achieving an outline residual of [7\.4 px]{.key} ([2\.03%]{.key} of mask scale). This matches the physical silhouette even more tightly than the in-flight belly frame ([15\.1 px]{.key}, [2\.90%]{.key}). Both poses report valid convergence (`Pose: good`), though the solver notes each basin remains hedged because unmodelled details—wingtip ordnance, canopy frame thickness, and intake ducting—prevent residuals from dropping below the strict [1%]{.key} hedge threshold. The visual overlay confirms that no gross loft or planform errors were hidden by the belly view.
